All 52 distinct retail scenes resolve with zero unresolved ANIMATION values. Companion note: Z:/memRip/knowledge/gamecube/stb-animation-ids.md. Generated 2026-08-21.
rule: Feature 58 ANIMATION carries a u32 that dDemo_actor_c::JSGSetAnimation stores in mAnmId. Three different consumers read it back. (1) The player object named 'Link': the value is a daPy_demo_c::Mode_e enum, not a resource id; only 0x200 (DEMO_NEW_ANM0_e) plays a file from the .stb, and that file's resource id is the first u16 of the actor's JSGSetData record, looked up in res/Object/LkD00.arc (LkD01.arc late in the game). (2) A generic 'd_actN' actor (daDemo00_c): the id is cast to u16 and fetched from the scene's Demo%02d.arc. (3) Any named NPC or object actor: bit 0x10000 selects the archive - set = the scene's Demo%02d.arc, clear = the actor's own object archive - and the low 16 bits are the RARC file id of a .bck inside it.

namespaces.0x10000: bit 16 set: the low 16 bits are a RARC file id inside the Demo%02d.arc the cutscene was mounted from (dStage_roomControl_c::getDemoArcName(), set from the room's Lbnk bank in d_s_room.cpp:214). d_demo.cpp:160-163.
namespaces.plain: bit 16 clear: the value is a RARC file id inside the actor's OWN object archive - the i_arcName the actor hands to dDemo_setDemoData (d_demo.cpp:164-166). For 'Link' a plain value is instead a daPy_demo_c mode enum and no resource is fetched at all. For 'd_actN' the bit is irrelevant: daDemo00_c masks to u16 and always uses the Demo arc (d_a_demo00.cpp:230 and 323).
namespaces.0x10000000: a DIFFERENT bit, and only on the BTK/BRK ids daDemo00_c reads out of its data records: it means 'loop and keep the current frame' (d_a_demo00.cpp:363-365, 386-392). It never appears on a BCK id.

resource_id_semantics: the low 16 bits are the RARC file-entry id (the u16 at offset 0 of each 0x14-byte file entry), resolved by JKRArchive::findIdResource through mDoExt_resIDToIndex (m_Do_ext.cpp:1117) and dRes_control_c::getIDRes (d_resorce.cpp:677). It is NOT a linear index into the file list, although the two happen to coincide in most TWW archives. gcrip.formats.rarc exposes it as RarcFile.file_id.

data_records.what: paragraph type 0x81 -> JSGSetData(id, blob, size) -> dDemo_actor_c::mPrm (d_demo.cpp:205-210). The blob is a JStudio::stb::data::TParse_TParagraph_data chain (stb-data-parse.cpp:51-79): u8 status; if (status & 8) a u8 count follows, else count = 1; then count elements of gauDataSize_TEParagraph_data[status & 7] bytes each; a 0 status ends the chain. The status a parser reports is (raw & ~8), which is exactly what TParseData_fixed<50,u16>, <49,u8>, <51,u32> and <33,s8> assert on.
data_records.link: daPy_lk_c::dProcTool, d_a_player_dproc.inc:196-330. data id 0/2/4 -> TParseData_fixed<50,u16> holding ONE u16 = the BCK file id in LkD00.arc. data id 1/3/5 -> the same record holding THREE u16 = [bck id, btp id, btk id]; the btp/btk pair is passed to setDemoTextureAnime. A TParseData_fixed<49,u8> follows: 2 entries = [left-hand item, right-hand item], 3 entries = [left, right, morf frames]. ids 2/3 also raise mProcVar7, ids 4/5 raise mProcVar3. The BCK is read with JKRReadIdResource(buf, 0xB400, id, dComIfGp_getLkDemoAnmArchive()) at d_a_player_dproc.inc:312.
data_records.npc: dDemo_actor_c::getP_BtpData / getP_BtkData / getP_BrkData (d_demo.cpp:54-68) are Nonmatching stubs in the decomp, so this part is read off the disc rather than out of code: data id 4 = one u32 = a BTP id; data id 5 = two u32 = [BTP id, BTK id]; both use the same 0x10000 archive-select namespace as ANIMATION. An optional trailing u8 record holds the morf (blend) frame count, and dDemo_actor_c::getPrm_Morf (d_demo.cpp:71-111) reads exactly that byte: prm id 1 -> offset 4, 2 -> 7, 4 -> 6, 5 -> 0xB, 6 -> 0xF - each of which is the value byte of the trailing record for that record shape. Verified: Zl1 in meet_tetra carries 3b 02 00010045 0001004e 31 14, so morf = 0x14 = 20 frames.
data_records.demo00: daDemo00_c, d_a_demo00.cpp:645-800, treats the data id as a command instead: 4 = set an event bit, 5 = give an item, 6 = monotone rate, 7 = rumble, 9/10 = fade out/in in black/white; anything else is parsed as TParseData_fixed<51,u32> read as (selector, value) pairs (:788-806) where selector 0 = BTP id, 1 = BTK id, 2 = plight id, 3 = field_0x1C, 4 = BRK id.

Link.note: ANIMATION is a daPy_demo_c::Mode_e enum, NOT a resource id. 0x200 (DEMO_NEW_ANM0_e) means 'tool demo': the real BCK id is the FIRST u16 of the actor's JSGSetData record (data ids 0-5) and is a RARC file id in res/Object/LkD00.arc (LkD01.arc after event flag UNK_2D01). Any other value selects a hard-coded player proc via mDemoProcInitFuncTable[mode], which picks its own animation from code and ignores the data record.

unresolved: ANIMATION: nothing - every value in all 52 distinct retail .stb scenes resolves to a real .bck.

getP_BtpData/getP_BtkData/getP_BrkData are Nonmatching stubs, so the 'data id 4 = BTP, data id 5 = [BTP, BTK]' reading is inferred from name correlation on disc (awake.stb Ls1 ANIMATION 65603 = bcks/47_ls_bwait_l.bck alongside data id 5 = [btp/47_ls_bwait_l.btp, btk/47_ls_bwait_l.btk]), not read from source.
Gnd's data id 6 (three u32) is unexplained - d_a_gnd.cpp is a stub.
LkD00 vs LkD01 is chosen at runtime by event flag UNK_2D01 (d_s_play.cpp:1241); the link_arc recorded per scene here is whichever archive actually contains the ids.
own-archive names for Gnd / Ym1 / Ym2 / p_zelda / Bms2 are unknown (actors not decompiled), but none of them ever uses a plain ANIMATION value, so nothing is lost.
counter.stb (A_nami / VrTest, the only .stb outside a Demo arc) has no actor ANIMATION values at all.
